newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH MUNICIPALITIES' FINANCES TIGHTER IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH MUNICIPALITIES' FINANCES TIGHTER IN 1997.

text.p: Finnish municipalities expect their finances to be more strained this year than in 1996, Statistics Finland (SF) said on Wednesday in a statement.

"Increased tax revenues will not be sufficient to offset growth of expenditures and the decline in state grants, and annual operating surpluses are expected to fall by a total of three billion markka from last year," SF said.
Municipalities' operating surpluses per capita are expected to fall to 430 markka from last year's budgeted figure of 1,024 markka As income financing declines, borrowing will increase, SF said.
Net borrowing by municipalities would total some 1.2 billion markka this year, it said, noting that in 1996, local governments were net repayers of debt.
Municipalities estimate their tax revenues this year at 62.8 billion markka, or a good four billion markka more than last year, SF said.
Municipal investment is increasing gradually, with 12 billion markka budgeted for investment this year up from about eight billion markka in the depths of the early 1990s recession, SF said.
